emergent.summary: Today's event ticket offers a dead-end pair: 'View bill' opens the Plan workspace, and the ticket always says no evidence is attached (OS-093)
emergent.why: Two defects confirmed by reading the code, reported together by the owner from his phone ('it says no evidence is attached to this event and has a view bill link, the link just brings you to the plan page'). Every bill event's `detailHref` is the literal `/meridian?workspace=plan` (`meridian/services/dial.py:440`, and the same literal at :487 and :534), so the control labelled 'View bill' (`dial.js:1125`) delivers a workspace landing page rather than the bill; and `evidenceIds` is a hard-coded empty list (`dial.py:439`, :486), so `dial.js:1118` states 'No evidence is attached to this event' for a bill even where Plan already holds invoice evidence for it. The destination is a product decision rather than a bug fix: a deep link that focuses the bill, an in-place sheet, or leaving Plan as the landing page and rewording the control so it stops promising a bill -- the last is legitimate and free, and choosing it is the owner's call.

emergent.summary: The reported 'double ticket' layout problem on Today's Eversource bill was NOT reproduced, so it is recorded rather than fixed
emergent.why: The owner reported it in the same message as OS-093: 'the double ticket eversource bill looks messy where the text is placed, overlapping with the line between the two tickets'. A synthetic model shaped like the reported case -- an Eversource bill with a stated funding schedule (the long '$29.89/event, Crew's own estimate, due Sep 20 for Veterans Home' note), no evidence attached, a detailHref, plus a coexisting 'Eversource Payment Arrangement' bill in the same horizon -- measured ZERO text-box overlaps, ZERO nodes escaping the ticket's own border box, and exactly ONE `.obs-evidence-ticket` on the page, at 420x912 and 1440x900 (tmp/probe_today_ticket.py). The first fixture attempt used wrong field names (`perEventAmount`/`dueDate` instead of `contribution`/`deadline`) and rendered none of the long text, so it was re-measured rather than reported. Not reproducing a defect is not evidence that it is absent, and guessing at a visual defect is how a fix lands on the wrong element -- so this half needs the owner's screenshot, or the date and bill he had selected.
